steps.note: Sent by the kit once the app has started, from every MapWebhook. The platform tells Edge at once, so the hook is open without waiting for Edge's next poll.
The device sends no session and no cookie. Edge admits a POST to a declared hook even on a private app; anything else still needs sign-in. Address and signature illustrative.

steps.code:
# On the device: sign the exact bytes it sends, with the shared secret.
BODY='{"court":"3","occupied":true}'
printf '%s' "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SENSOR_SECRET"
steps.note: The kit reads SENSOR_SECRET from the vault, computes HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, strips the optional sha256= prefix from the header and compares in constant time. The output format is OpenSSL's.
The handler runs only after the call verified. ReadJson<T>() reads camelCase JSON; ReadText() gives the body as text; Body is the raw bytes exactly as signed.

body.title: Webhook verification failed
body.detail: The X-Signature header did not verify.

steps.note: A missing header, a wrong prefix, bad hex or a wrong MAC all end here, and the handler never runs. The problem also carries a traceId.
Verification asks the vault for SENSOR_SECRET; EndgameSecretNotFoundException reaches the kit's error handler. Set the secret with SEC-03. Plus a traceId.
Only a hand-made call can send another path; MapWebhook always uses hooks/<name>. Also refused: "An app declares at most 50 webhooks." and "Two webhooks have the same name."
